Android 可能很快就会限制设备上的 ADB

Android may soon restrict on-device ADB

科技产品 作者 shscs911 热度 1000 回复 501 2026/07/25 14:57
打开原帖 打开外部链接 JSON

摘要

  • Android 可能限制设备端 ADB 连接，以防范恶意行为者。
  • 该变化可能影响依赖本地 ADB 的开源项目（如 Shizuku）及开发者工作流。
  • 作者呼吁社区提供建设性反馈，避免在 IssueTracker 上发布低质量评论。

看点

  • Android 计划限制设备端 ADB 连接，旨在提升系统安全性。
  • Shizuku 等开源项目可能受到直接影响，开发者需关注后续更新。
  • 作者分享了个人使用场景，强调无障碍功能对特殊用户的重要性。
  • 社区被鼓励通过 IssueTracker 提供详细反馈，而非简单抱怨。
  • ADB 的多种连接方式（USB、TCP/IP、无线调试）及其技术背景被详细解析。

帖子讨论了 Android 可能限制设备端 ADB 连接的计划，涉及 Android 开发工具、系统安全策略及开源社区项目（如 Shizuku），与科技产品和开发工具高度相关。

microtonal 2026/07/25 16:14
我总体上赞成改进安全性，但我并没有真正看到这里有什么好处。此攻击媒介要求用户启用开发人员设置并且启用远程 adb。因此，对于 99.9% 的用户来说，这似乎不是一个现实的攻击媒介，而其他 0.1% 的大多数用户可能知道他们在做什么。

另一个提议的更改（限制对某些接口或 IP 地址的访问）似乎不错，但为什么不允许开发人员限制访问 localhost？

它散发着试图阻止 Shizuku、Canta 等的味道，使用的方式只会使其看起来像副作用。

I am generally in favor of security improvements, but I do not really see much of a benefit here. This attack vector requires both that the user enabled developer settings and that they have remote adb enabled. So, this does not seem to be a realistic attack vector for 99.9% of the users and most of the other 0.1% probably know what they are doing.

The other proposed change (to restrict access to certain interfaces or IP addresses) seems good, but why not allow developers to restrict access localhost?

It reeks of trying to block Shizuku, Canta, etc. using a way that only makes it look like a side-effect.

AnthonyMouse 2026/07/26 03:32
有一个简单且高度准确的启发式方法可以判断安全措施是否合理：

它是任何人都可以无需许可实施的开放标准吗？

当答案是肯定时，很可能它是合理的，例如TOTP。

当答案是否定的时，你会发现幕后的人要么是傻子，要么是骗子。

There is a simple and highly accurate heuristic to tell if a security measure is reasonable:

Is it an open standard that anyone can permissionlessly implement?

When the answer is yes, there is a high probability that it's something reasonable, e.g. TOTP.

When the answer is no, what you will find behind the curtain is either a fool or a crook.

TeMPOraL 2026/07/26 04:26
这种启发式方法没有涵盖这里感兴趣的维度，因为它无法解决关键的安全问题（业界通常希望人们根本不去思考这些问题）：

谁在进行安全保护，谁的利益受到保护，以及针对谁/什么？

安全并不是一件绝对好的事情。它只是一个控制工具。谁运用它以及如何运用它是最重要的问题。您可以拥有一个“任何人都可以在未经许可的情况下实施的开放标准”，旨在通过保护设备免受其实际所有者的侵害来保护第三方的利益。事实上，这描述了过去 20 年计算领域引入的许多（如果不是大多数）安全措施，尤其是在网络和移动设备上。

This heuristic is not covering the dimensions of interest here, because it fails to address the key security questions (that the industry usually wants people to not even think about):

Who is doing the securing, whose interests are being secured, and against who/what?

Security isn't an unqualified good thing to have. It's just an instrument of control. Who wields it and how are the paramount questions. You can have an "open standard that anyone can permissionlessly implement", aimed at protecting interest of third parties, by securing the device from its actual owner. In fact, that describes many, if not most, security measures introduced in computing over the past 20 years, especially on the web and mobile devices.

> 您可以拥有一个“任何人都可以无需许可地实施的开放标准”，旨在通过保护设备免受其实际所有者的侵害来保护第三方的利益。

但您不能，因为这些系统要求设备附带密钥，因此可互操作的第三方实现需要密钥，而这需要许可，而这正是“无许可”想要驱逐的东西。

> You can have an "open standard that anyone can permissionlessly implement", aimed at protecting interest of third parties, by securing the device from its actual owner.

Except that you can't, because those systems require the device to come with secret keys, so an interoperable third party implementation would require keys, which requires permission, which is the exact thing "permissionless" is intended to evict.

几十年来，安全领域已经众所周知，为了“安全”而采取安全性/可用性权衡是训练用户从肌肉记忆中按下“允许所有”按钮的快速方法，从而严重损害安全性。

可怕横幅的前提必须是用户第一次看到它时确实出现了问题。

当然，这与公司激励完全不相容。每当诚实的第三方没有向他们支付丹麦金或满足弗朗茨·卡夫卡记录的官僚程序时，就展示可怕的横幅。如果您关心的实际上是安全性。

It has been a known thing in security for what has to be decades now that taking a security/usability trade off in favor of "security" is the fast way to train users to mash the "allow all" button from muscle memory, thereby severely impairing security.

The premise of the scary banner has to be that the first time the user has ever seen it is when there is actually something wrong.

This is, of course, fully incompatible with the corporate incentive to present the scary banner whenever an honest third party hasn't paid them the danegeld or satisfied a bureaucratic process documented by Franz Kafka. If the thing you care about is actually security.

TeMPOraL 2026/07/27 05:45
不，如果网站从一开始就不重要，那么它就不会变得重要。这不以个别用例为条件。政府站点、您的银行、您的医疗保健提供者——他们都有重要的站点。您的电子邮件提供商也很重要，因为由于互联网历史的偶然，您的电子邮件是您数字生活中所有内容的备份密钥。

除此之外，没有什么那么重要。您随机的电子商务网站或讨论区并不那么重要。您的 ISP 或您修理设备（或电话）的服务也不是。尤其是那些随机的、不可靠的初创公司，他们希望你在测试他们的“改变游戏规则”的 SaaS 之前注册。

可悲的讽刺是，网站越小、越不重要，他们往往部署越严格的安全措施，因为安全剧院现在很流行。 2FA 已经到了 2025 年了，如果你不要求密钥，你就是恐龙。

（这是一个很好的启发式方法：如果你的网站比政府的核心服务具有更严格的安全性，特别是在恢复访问时，那么值得问问是否有任何真正合理的理由。）

No, the site doesn't become important if it wasn't from the start. This is not conditioned on individual use cases. Government sites, your bank, your healthcare provider - they have the important sites. Your e-mail provider is important too, because by accident of Internet history, your e-mail is your backup key to everything in your digital life.

Beyond those, nothing is that important. Your random e-commerce site or discussion board are not that important. Neither is your ISP or the service where you fix your appliances (or phones). And especially not the random fly-by-night startups that want you to register before you test their "game changing" SaaS.

The sad irony is, the smaller and less important the site, the more stringent security measures they tend to deploy, because security theater is trendy nowadays. 2FA is so 2025, if you're not demanding passkeys, you're a dinosaur.

(A good heuristic to use: if your site has harder security than your government's core services, especially when it comes to recovering access, it's worth asking whether there's any actually sensible reason for it.)
